title: Studio Access pillar: package-level OWD overview — audit & batch-edit sharingModel across all objects in a package
body:
# Problem

For a **package author**, the record-sharing baseline (OWD, `sharingModel` / `externalSharingModel`) of the package's objects can only be inspected and edited **one object at a time**, via the Data pillar → object → *Settings* tab (`ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx`). The permission matrix (`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`) shows a read-only OWD badge per object row, but offers no way to change it and no package-wide view.

Consequences:

- A package with 20 objects requires opening 20 settings pages to audit its baseline posture. In practice this means nobody audits it: in the `com.example.showcase` dogfood app, most objects sit at `public_read_write` while a few are `private`, and this imbalance is invisible from any single screen.
- ADR-0090 D1 made explicit OWD mandatory precisely because the silent-widening failure class (objectui#2348) is invisible object-by-object. A per-object-only editing surface leaves the *review* side of that decision unsupported: there is no screen on which "which of my objects are org-wide writable?" can be answered at a glance.
- The `externalSharingModel ≤ sharingModel` constraint (ADR-0090 D11) is validated per object at authoring/lint time, but an author can't survey the external dimension across the package before publish.

# Proposal

Add a package-scoped **"Record Sharing Baseline (OWD)" panel** to the Studio **Access pillar**, as a sibling surface next to the permission-set rail (not inside the permission matrix):

- A table of **object × `sharingModel` × `externalSharingModel`** covering every object owned by the current package (published ∪ pending drafts, same merge the pillars already do).
- Inline select per cell using the canonical four values (`private | public_read | public_read_write | controlled_by_parent`), reusing the option labels/help copy from `ObjectSettingsPanel` and the badge/i18n helpers from `views/metadata-admin` (`owdLabel`, `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`).
- `controlled_by_parent` rows display the master link (read-only) instead of an external dial, mirroring the per-object settings behavior.
- Row-level validation `external ≤ internal` (the `OWD_WIDTH` comparison already implemented in `ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx`) surfaced inline before save.
- **Save = per-object metadata drafts** under the package scope — exactly what the per-object Settings tab writes today, just N objects in one action. Publish then flows through the existing security-domain gate unchanged (ADR-0090 D7 lint + human gate; the D6 semantic diff is naturally per-row: "`showcase_contact` widens `private` → `public_read`").
- Deep-linkable via the existing `?surface=` plumbing (`useSurfaceDeepLink`), so the read-only OWD badge in the permission matrix can link here.

## Why this does not blur the ADR-0090 concept boundaries

Merging OWD into the *permission-set* matrix was considered and rejected (ADR-0090; permission sets are additive per-principal unions, OWD is a per-object scalar baseline with a different owner). This proposal is **not** that: every row in this table has the **same owner — the package author** ("OWD: object author · sharing: environment", `docs/design/permission-model.md`). It is an aggregation of N editing entry points *within one ownership boundary*, not a merge of two concepts. It has no principal dimension and binds to nobody.

# Non-goals

- **No package-level default OWD with inheritance.** The table batch-edits N *explicit* per-object values. A package default that objects inherit would reintroduce the ambient "unset" state ADR-0090 D1 abolished.
- **Not merging OWD editing into the permission-set matrix.** The matrix keeps its read-only badge (now linkable).
- **`enable.*` capability switches are out of scope.** The same ownership argument supports a package-level "object × capability switch" overview, but those are behavior config, not authorization — if pursued, it belongs in the Data pillar as a follow-up issue.
- No changes to enforcement, lint rules, or the publish pipeline — this is purely an authoring-surface addition.

# Implementation notes

- **Entry point**: `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `AccessPillar` (rail pattern, `?surface=` deep-link, `publishNonce` re-read after publish are all established there).
- **Reuse**: OWD select options + external-dial + `OWD_WIDTH` validation from `views/studio-design/ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx` (likely extract a shared control); OWD label/i18n from `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`.
- **Data**: `client.list('object', { packageId })` ∪ `client.listDrafts({ packageId, type: 'object' })`; per-object draft save on batch apply; OCC / destructive-change dialog conventions per the existing editors.
- Read-only mode must follow the pillar's `readOnly` courtesy gate (package read-only ⇒ table renders badges only).

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Access pillar shows an OWD overview listing **all** objects of the current package (published ∪ drafts) with internal + external sharing model per row.
- [ ] Author can change multiple objects' OWD and save once; each change lands as that object's package-scoped draft; publish goes through the unchanged security-domain gate.
- [ ] `external > internal` is blocked inline per row; `controlled_by_parent` rows show the master and no external dial.
- [ ] The OWD badge in `PermissionMatrixEditor` deep-links to this panel.
- [ ] Read-only packages render the table non-editable.
- [ ] ADR-0054 testability proofs for the new surface (list render, edit→draft, validation block, deep-link).

# References

- framework ADR-0090 (Permission Model v2 — D1 mandatory explicit OWD, D4 canonical enum, D11 external dial, D6 explain / D7 security-domain gate) and companion `docs/design/permission-model.md`
- objectui ADR-0056 (permission editing belongs in Studio — "one validated authoring path per concern")
- objectui#2348 (OWD control in Studio + dogfood incident), objectui#2403 (structured permission editors)

_Origin: Studio dogfooding of `com.example.showcase` — auditing the package's record baseline currently requires visiting every object's settings page individually._
